example: In `src/lib.rs`, a method `run` in `impl Thing` has selector `impl[Thing]/fn[run]`; a method `run` in `impl Trait for Thing` has selector `impl[Thing/Trait]/fn[run]`; and a method `read` declared in `trait Read` has selector `trait[Read]/fn[read]`. {cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_selectors`
rationale:
Two tests carry `{test}` references to this example, in `src/outline/tests.rs`. The references tool confirms both.

**Scenario:** An inherent-impl method has selector `impl[Thing]/fn[run]`. A trait-impl method has selector `impl[Thing/Trait]/fn[run]`. A trait-declared method has selector `trait[Read]/fn[read]`.

**`rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` (line 35):**
- Its source has `struct Thing; impl Thing { fn run() {} }`, `impl Trait for Thing { fn run() {} }` and `trait Trait { fn read(&self); ... }`. It outlines them as `src/lib.rs`, the file named in the example.
- It asserts that the selector list contains `impl[Thing]/fn[run]`, `impl[Thing/Trait]/fn[run]` and `trait[Trait]/fn[read]`.
- It also asserts that `outline.resolve(selector)` returns a node whose selector equals the one asked for, so resolution works as well as generation.

**`selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` (line 520):**
- It repeats the same three assertions on a separate source, using `lib.rs`.
- The same source places `impl Thing` and `impl Trait for Thing` side by side, so the tests show the two impls get different selectors.

The tests use the trait name `Trait` instead of the example's `Read`. This does not matter, because the selector format (`impl[Self/Trait]`, `trait[Name]`) is what the example specifies. Together the tests cover all three selector shapes in the example, and also the neighbouring cases of generic and array self types and duplicates.

The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
